audioScript: Welcome to gallery 4 of the Ashcombe Museum, and to our exhibition on the history of papermaking. The object in front of you is a hand press built in 1794, a century after the first paper mills opened along this river. Notice the wooden screw at the top; turning it pressed damp fibers against a felt sheet, and a skilled worker could produce about 200 sheets in a day. The press was donated by the Hartley family in 1962, when the last mill in the region closed, and it stood outdoors in the courtyard for 30 years before our conservation team spent 4 years restoring it. Please do not touch the press, as the oils on your fingers can damage the wood. The next room continues with machine-made paper, and the film there starts every 15 minutes.
